blocks.text: 22 תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית 22
לג
רַנְּנוּ צַדִּיקִים בַּיהוָה לַיְשָׁרִים נָאוָה תְהִלָּה:
הוֹדוּ לַיהוָה בְּכִנּוֹר בְּנֵבֶל עָשׂוֹר זַמְּרוּ־לוֹ:
שִׁירוּ לוֹ שִׁיר חָדָשׁ הֵיטִיבוּ נַגֵּן בִּתְרוּעָה:
כִּי־יָשָׁר דְּבַר־יְהוָה וְכָל־מַעֲשֵׂהוּ בֶּאֱמוּנָה:
אֹהֵב צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט חֶסֶד יְהוָה מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ:
בִּדְבַר יְהוָה שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ וּבְרוּחַ פִּיו כָּל־צְבָאָם:
כֹּנֵס כַּנֵּד מֵי הַיָּם נֹתֵן בְּאוֹצָרוֹת תְּהוֹמוֹת:
יִירְאוּ מֵיְהוָה כָּל־הָאָרֶץ מִמֶּנּוּ יָגוּרוּ כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל:
כִּי הוּא אָמַר וַיֶּהִי הוּא צִוָּה וַיַּעֲמֹד:
יְהוָה הֵפִיר עֲצַת גּוֹיִם הֵנִיא מַחְשְׁבוֹת עַמִּים:
עֲצַת יְהוָה לְעוֹלָם תַּעֲמֹד מַחְשְׁבוֹת לִבּוֹ לְדֹר וָדֹר:
אַשְׁרֵי הַגּוֹי אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָה אֱלֹהָיו הָעָם בָּחַר לְנַחֲלָה לוֹ:
מִשָּׁמַיִם הִבִּיט יְהוָה רָאָה אֶת־כָּל־בְּנֵי הָאָדָם:
מִמְּכוֹן שִׁבְתּוֹ הִשְׁגִּיחַ אֶל כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ:
הַיֹּצֵר יַחַד לִבָּם הַמֵּבִין אֶל־כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם:
אֵין הַמֶּלֶךְ נוֹשָׁע בְּרָב־חָיִל גִּבּוֹר לֹא־יִנָּצֵל בְּרָב־כֹּחַ:
שֶׁקֶר הַסּוּס לִתְשׁוּעָה וּבְרֹב
22 Morning Prayer 22
(Psalm 33.)
Exult, O righteous ones, in the Lord, it is becoming to the upright to give praise.
Thank the Lord with the zither, with the ten-stringed harp make music to Him.
Sing to Him a new song, pluck the strings well in triumph.
For upright is the word of the Lord and all His work is with faithfulness.
He loves righteousness and justice, the grace of the Lord fills the earth.
Through the word of the Lord were the heavens made and through the breath of His mouth all their host.
He gathers like a heap the waters of the seas, and puts the depths into store-chambers.
The whole earth is afraid before the Lord, before Him do all inhabitants of the world tremble.
For He spoke and it was, He commanded and there it stood.
The Lord has frustrated the plan of nations, baffled the thoughts of peoples.
The counsel of the Lord endures for ever, the thoughts of His heart from generation to generation.
Fortunate the nation whose God is the Lord, the people which He has chosen as His inheritance.
The Lord has looked from heaven, He has seen all the sons of man.
From His dwelling place does He watch over all the inhabitants of the earth.
He who has formed their hearts altogether, He understands all their deeds.
The king is not saved by the size of an army, the warrior will not escape through the measure of strength.
Useless is the horse for victory, by the measure of its might
23 תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית 23
חֵילוֹ לֹא יְמַלֵּט:
הִנֵּה עֵין יְהוָה אֶל־יְרֵאָיו לַמְיַחֲלִים לְחַסְדּוֹ:
לְהַצִּיל מִמָּוֶת נַפְשָׁם וּלְחַיּוֹתָם בָּרָעָב:
נַפְשֵׁנוּ חִכְּתָה לַיהוָה עֶזְרֵנוּ וּמָגִנֵּנוּ הוּא:
כִּי־בוֹ יִשְׂמַח לִבֵּנוּ כִּי בְשֵׁם קָדְשׁוֹ בָטָחְנוּ:
יְהִי־חַסְדְּךָ יְהוָה עָלֵינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר יִחַלְנוּ לָךְ:
23 Morning Prayer 23
it will not save.
Behold, the eye of the Lord is towards those who fear Him, those who wait for His grace.
To save their soul from death and to keep them alive in famine.
Our soul has waited for the Lord, He is our help and our shield.
In Him will our heart rejoice, for in His holy Name do we trust.
May Thy grace be upon us, O Lord, since we have waited for Thee.

uncertainties.issue: In the bands I could not see a separate holam dot above the vav in any Name, so they are transcribed as יְהוָה / בַּיהוָה / לַיהוָה / מֵיְהוָה without holam. The vav heads are thick, so a holam merged into the vav head can't be ruled out at this resolution. Each Name needs checking at higher magnification.
There is a small looped or circular mark at the bottom of this Name, under or next to the final he. It may be a cantillation or meteg-like sign, or a print blemish. It is not transcribed.
There is an extra small stroke or mark near the final ח, possibly a stress or accent sign or a blemish. It is not transcribed.
The dagesh in the first nun and the sheva under it are faint. I've transcribed them as רַנְּנוּ, but רַנְנוּ (without the dagesh) is possible.
Both the dagesh in the mem and the maqaf between זַמְּרוּ and לוֹ are unclear. The line may read זַמְרוּ לוֹ or זַמְּרוּ לוֹ, without the maqaf.
The holam on the alef is faint or touches the letter top. I read it as present.
The holam dots on the כ and the נ are faint. I read them as present.
The holam on the yod is not clearly separate from the yod head in either occurrence.

uncertainties.scope: 33/9 s74, וַיַּעֲמֹד; 33/11 s74, תַּעֲמֹד and לְדֹר וָדֹר
uncertainties.issue: The holam dots on מ/ד are small. I read them as present.
The maqaf between כָּל and בְּנֵי is faint. I read it as present.
There is no maqaf after אֶל. I've kept this as printed; it is not an omission on my part.
Small marks below letters (e.g. under הֵיטִיבוּ, מַעֲשֵׂהוּ, וַיֶּהִי) may be meteg or stress marks. I could not identify them reliably at band resolution, so none are transcribed.

observations: The Hebrew chapter marker לג is a small sign at the start of the first line of 33/1 on s74. The English citation is '(Psalm 33.)' at the start of the paragraph on s75. Both are recorded as citation blocks, not as prayer text.

The page break falls inside 33/17 in both languages. Hebrew: s74 ends 'וּבְרֹב' and s76 starts 'חֵילוֹ לֹא יְמַלֵּט:'. English: s75 ends 'by the measure of its might' and s77 starts 'it will not save.'
The line-final maqaf in 33/8 on s74 (…מֵיְהוָה כָּל־ | הָאָרֶץ) is a real maqaf. It is kept and the words are joined across the line break.
'ten-stringed' (33/2) and 'store-chambers' (33/7) fall mid-line on s75, so their hyphens are real compounds. Neither English page has any line-break hyphenation inside Psalm 33.
There is a stray dot below 'righteous' in 33/1 on s75. It looks like a scan blemish and is not transcribed.
Psalm 33 ends at 'לָךְ:' and 'for Thee.' The text after that on s76/s77 is Psalm 92 (marked צב / '(Psalm 92.)') and is excluded. The Psalm 136 lines above Psalm 33 on s74/s75 are also excluded.
